facts.v: Every brand visit since 19 Sep has come in under usual on all three counts: likes, comments and plays. Eight in a row.
Only 2 of the 13 brand visits have beaten usual, and both did it on every count.

bulletin.learned: A brand visit lands only when the brand is the backdrop to a sketch @anuj.mp4 would have made anyway. Both that landed were built that way.
bulletin.why: A brand visit puts @anuj.mp4 in someone else's room, on someone else's script: a launch party, a showroom, a studio poster. The jokes that work on this account need @anuj.mp4 to be the one in trouble, and at a brand's event nobody is. facts.v: Five protest reels in twelve days, every one above usual on likes and on comments. None since 14 Oct.
The 12-second reel has 867,907 likes and 3,416 comments, the most of both in 90 days, from 9.9 million plays.
Two of the five were played no more than a usual reel and still drew three to six times the likes and comments.

bulletin.learned: The sharpest work on this account is unsponsored, topical and short. It earns its likes and comments without needing the plays, and it is the first thing to disappear.
bulletin.why: These reels are @anuj.mp4 at full pitch: one double standard, acted out in under half a minute, with no setup and no sponsor. The 12-second one is the purest version, the same government shown twice, back to back. They came while the protests were in the news, and they stopped the week brand posts took over the feed.

bulletin.label: Losing streak · the whole account
bulletin.head: Followers down nine days running.

facts.v: 1,515 followers gone between 19 and 27 Oct, with a loss every single day.
A usual day adds about 124. The longest losing run before this was 4 days.

facts.k: What went up in those days
facts.v: A product review, six posts from a trip to Japan and three more brand reels. Two are old enough to judge: the review fell under usual on all three counts, and the breakup skit beat usual on likes and comments.

bulletin.learned: The count held while the account had a point of view, and slid when it had a client list.
bulletin.why: Nothing says which post did it. What the nine days share is what was missing. No politics, no calls, and nothing a visitor could not get from an ad: a product review, holiday footage, three sponsored reels. The two acts that built this account were both off the feed at once.

facts.v: Five brand reels in seven weeks were played 6 to 137 times usual. Not one got past 1.2 times usual on likes in its first week.
The Cadbury reel was played 22.6 million times, more than twice the two-faces reel, and had 4,030 likes after a week.
Its likes then grew ninefold by day 21, while its comments went from 149 to 157.

bulletin.learned: Plays that big with likes that late is the pattern of a paid push. Comments moved on only two of the five, so on a brand reel comments are the count to trust.
bulletin.why: When a reel works here, all three counts climb together, as they did on the two-faces reel. On these five the plays ran far ahead alone. The Gemini one spends a minute on a phone assistant planning a Garba night, and there is no joke in it to like or argue with.

drops.world: @anuj.mp4 is a Mumbai comedy creator working in Hinglish, mixing sketches, split-screen calls with @shreeecreates, direct-to-camera pleas and brand work. The account's own vocabulary is its pieces (Shree calls, Named-person pleas, Protest satire, Flex reels, Brand sketches), its props (the black Versace robe, cash, watches and chains) and its rooms, mostly a home and a desk. Outside the account it draws on Indian politics and protest news, Premier League football and the Matchday Hangout broadcast, film and TV references, festivals and the brands it is hired by. Paid labels, #ad tags and collaborator handles mark the brand work.

1.title: The pair works at war and dies of kindness
1.line: @anuj.mp4 and @shreeecreates play a couple on a video call who cannot stop fighting. Ten calls since 2 Sep. None in the last 16 days.

shape.card: @anuj.mp4 and @shreeecreates play a couple on a video call who cannot stop fighting. Ten calls since 2 Sep. None in the last 16 days.
shape.read: The fight was the product. Without it there is no act.

stages.name: Everything
findings: This pair is chaos and madness in equal parts. @anuj.mp4 demands money back and gets baby faces in reply. Two eggs earn a slipper thrown from one screen into the other. A grandfather is called in as backup and the slaps keep coming. [[P032|The money call]], [[P043|The egg call]] and [[P045|The sleep check]] are three of the biggest things this account has made, and nine of the ten calls landed.
Then the pair went sweet, the response shrank, and the calls stopped.

stages.name: Evolving
findings: Affection does not work for these two. The month's two calls were [[P076|A cheerful product review]] and [[P096|A friendly duet]], and both passed almost unnoticed.

Look back over all ten and it is plain: the harder the fight, the bigger the response. The slipper, the shouting and the bedtime bickering sit at the top. The duet, the review and the sing-along sit at the bottom.

stages.name: Emerging
findings: Nothing again. Two weeks in a row now, the longest gap since the pair began. If the calls come back, they need to come back swinging.

shape.riding: Each call picks up the last. The catchphrase from the first comes back in the third, and [[P057|The late-night scolding]] is the sleep check played again.
shape.recommend: What works: the two at each other's throats over nothing. What does not: the two being nice. Still unknown: whether the act is finished or only resting.

shape.card: A reel's plays set beside its likes and comments. Five reels were played far more than they were liked, and all five were made for brands.
shape.read: The brand reels travel; the reels people care about stay close to home and get liked hard. On this account likes and comments are the counts to trust.

stages.name: Everything
findings: The gap opened with [[P046|The Cadbury brownie]]: a robe, a gold spoon and a sprint round the living room. It was played 22.6 million times, 137 times a usual reel, and its likes after a week were ordinary. Three weeks on the likes had grown ninefold. The comments had gone from 149 to 157.
The calls with @shreeecreates ran the other way. [[P045|The sleep check]] was liked eight times over on three times the plays.

stages.name: Evolving
findings: It became a pattern. [[P075|The Redmi crime show]], a TV host narrating @anuj.mp4 dropping a phone, was played 15 million times and liked less than half as much as usual in its first week. [[P091|The Amazon price game]] was played 8 million times with fewer comments than a usual post.

In the same weeks the protest reels did the reverse. [[P094|The protest round-up]] had ordinary plays and nearly six times the likes. [[P092|Utha lete hain]] was liked 274 times over on 55 times the plays.

stages.name: Emerging
findings: Nothing to read yet: plays are counted once, after a reel's first week. Two brand reels went up on 27 Oct and are the next to check.

shape.riding: The brand reels lean on things people already know: a crime show and its real host, a price-guessing stream, a food review in a bathrobe.
shape.recommend: What the counts show: a reel made for a brand can be played in the millions here and leave almost no mark in likes or comments. What gets liked far past its plays is a short reel with a point of view: the protest satire and the calls. Still unknown: where the brand reels' plays come from. The counts cannot say.

1.title: Posting more has never been the answer here
1.line: @anuj.mp4 posts on about six days of every seven, usually twice a day. Ten to thirteen posts a week, almost without a break since mid August.

shape.card: @anuj.mp4 posts on about six days of every seven, usually twice a day. Ten to thirteen posts a week, almost without a break since mid August.
shape.read: The pace is steady, so it explains nothing. A good week and a bad week carry the same number of posts. What differs is how many of the slots go to brands.

stages.name: Everything
findings: Sixty-two posting days out of ninety, and on forty-one of them more than one post. The longest silence since mid August is six days.

Two posts on one day do not get in each other's way. The second lands as often as the first, and days with two or more do better than days with one. [[P043|The egg call]], the biggest post before October, went up on a day that already had a reel.

stages.name: Evolving
findings: Two weeks side by side tell it. The week to 13 Oct had twelve posts and eight landed, with [[P092|Utha lete hain]] and [[P098|The law degree]] in it. The week to 20 Oct had ten posts and two landed.
The pace was the same. Brands took three slots in the first week and five in the second, among them [[P106|The Nykaa review]].

stages.name: Emerging
findings: Twelve posts again, on six days, from a holiday in Japan. [[P114|Four peti of yen]], a street reel with a stack of cash, is ahead of usual after three days. [[P112|Day one in Japan]], a 96-second diary, is at half. Too early to call the week.

shape.riding: The news sets the best weeks: every protest reel came within days of the story breaking.
shape.recommend: What the counts show: posting twice a day costs nothing here, and the one quiet week did no better than the busy ones. What moves a week is what the posts are. Still unknown: time of day. The posting hour in this data cannot be trusted yet.

findings: Late August was the strongest stretch: more than 3,700 in a fortnight, with [[P010|The makeover duel]] up, the most liked post the account had had.

Nine days later the count began to fall, and it has not had an up day since: nine losing days in a row to 27 Oct.

findings: Down 1,359 this week, the worst week here. On the feed in those days: a Japan trip, [[P108|A night drive in the BMW]] and brand reels, among them [[P109|The Pierre Cardin therapy sketch]]. The calls and the protest reels, which were up in the weeks the count climbed, are absent.
